title: Higher levels of sexual dichromatism are associated with faster life history strategies and lower latitudes in passerine birds
content:
Abstract
Sexual dichromatism has been widely investigated in passerine birds, with studies looking at its relationship with life history traits and latitude. However, the relationship between sexual dichromatism and life history traits has yet to be established without the use of confounding proxies such as body size or latitude. Here, we compile five different measures of sexual dichromatism along with data relating to latitude, life history strategies, mating system and body mass for 205 passerine bird species and use phylogenetic comparative methods to test how the degree of sexual dichromatism relates to the fast–slow continuum of life history strategies while accounting for latitude, body mass, and mating system. We find support that species with faster life history strategies inhabiting lower latitudes and with mating systems associated with high levels of male competition have greater levels of sexual dichromatism. However, while we find support for each of these factors, we also find that support varies across the five measures of sexual dichromatism, highlighting the potential importance of metric choice in studies of sexual dichromatism. Overall, our results show that after accounting for confounding correlations, life history and latitude are likely to play a role in the evolution of sexual dichromatic features in passerines.
